scenes.headline: Reading a desktop as refs, not pixels
scenes.sub: How agent-desktop lets an agent use any app
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Teasel! This tool lets an agent read and operate a desktop app without looking at a picture of it.

scenes.text: Ask the operating system what is on screen, give each actionable element a short ref, and read only the region you need.
scenes.mark: give each actionable element a short ref
scenes.say: The operating system already describes every window as a tree. The tool gives each actionable element a ref, and the agent reads one region at a time.

steps.say: The agent runs snapshot, and the command line hands it to the core.
The core asks the platform adapter, which walks the operating system's accessibility tree.
Interactive elements get refs, saved in a ref map tied to that snapshot.
Then the agent acts on a ref, and reads again to check.

scenes.title: Map first, then open one region

items.say: A skeleton caps the depth at three, and marks every cut branch with how many children it hid.
Cut branches that can be found again get an anchor ref to open.
A drill re-reads only that region, and the rest of the snapshot stays valid.
Act on a ref, then read the same small region to verify.

scenes.say: A heavy app is read in two moves.

scenes.title: Tokens to look once at a chat app
scenes.say: On a toy chat app with one hundred and fifty messages, a full snapshot costs about twenty-four thousand tokens. One drill into a region costs two hundred.

left.title: Reading
left.say: Reading is concurrent, and each agent keeps its own snapshots in a session.

right.title: Acting
right.say: Acting is serialized. Input takes an interaction lease, so agents take turns to touch the app.

scenes.text: Read the tree in regions. A full snapshot of a heavy page can cost more than the screenshot it replaces.

scenes.say: Refs instead of pixels, a skeleton then a drill, and many agents that read while one acts.
